p.n: The Rat Distinguishes Hidden from Overt Enmity

body.p:
“The rat said:
‘Many a hidden enmity is, on the surface, a friendship, which is far more harmful
than open enmity,

and whoever is not wary of it will suffer that which befell the man
who rides the tusk of a rutting elephant, fell asleep, then wakes up beneath the feet of the elephant, who tramples
him to death.

p.n: An Enemy Is Befriended in Times of Need

body.p:
Now the friend is called a friend precisely for the benefits one hopes to gain from him,
and the enemy is called an enemy for the damage one fears from him; and when the sensible man hopes
to benefit from the enemy, he shows him friendship; and when he fears harm from a friend, he shows
him enmity.

p.n: Young Cattle Only Nurse for a While

body.p:

but when that milk stops flowing], they part from them Just

p.n: Enmity Turns into Friendship in Times of Need

body.p:

had allied him to his friend and not fear any evil from him, because the basis of the affair had not been enmity.
